We work closely with platform, infrastructure, ML systems, and product engineering teams to ensure that rapid iteration never comes at the expense of customer trust. Our environment spans distributed cloud systems, multi-region deployments, APIs, orchestration layers, and hardware-backed inference services.

We are scaling quickly. The systems are growing in complexity, traffic is increasing rapidly, and release velocity remains high. We need engineers who can build quality systems that scale with the business.

About The Role

As a Senior Software Engineer in Test for the ML API features team, you will lead testing strategy and execution for AI/ML models, evaluating accuracy, fairness, and performance at scale. You will serve as a key technical leader in delivering and validating all software and hardware components for Cerebras API Features. You will own software components feature integration quality and drive pre-deployment and production validation for Cerebras inference solutions. In this role, you will define and champion best testing practices, establish robust debugging methodologies, and mentor junior engineers while advocating for world-class product quality.

Responsibilities

 - Architect and own end-to-end test strategies for new features, developing scalable tests, frameworks, and tooling to ensure quality.

 - Lead contributions to industry-standard benchmarks and drive adoption of rigorous evaluation methodologies.

 - Define and drive automation initiatives to significantly improve internal engineering efficiency and test coverage.

 - Make strategic decisions around coverage trade-offs, resource requirements, and risk-based testing priorities.

 - Serve as a technical anchor in a highly agile environment, adapting quickly to shifting priorities while maintaining quality standards.

 - Mentor and guide junior SDETs on testing methodology, debugging practices, and automation development.

 - Proactively identify systemic quality gaps and drive cross-functional initiatives to address them.

 - Lead and facilitate effective technical communication across teams and time zones.

Skills & Qualifications

 - 5+ years of relevant industry experience in software integration, development, or quality engineering.

 - Deep expertise in automation and programming using one or more languages such as Python, C++, or Go; ability to design and build reusable test frameworks from the ground up.

 - Proven experience testing compute, machine learning, networking, or storage systems within large-scale enterprise environments.

 - Strong track record of debugging complex issues across distributed, scaled-out deployments.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional quality initiatives involving product development, product management, customer operations, and field teams.

 - Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with experience presenting technical findings to both engineering and leadership audiences.

 - Strong organizational skills, ownership mindset, and ability to drive projects to completion independently.

 - Experience leading and mentoring engineers across geographically dispersed teams and time zones.

Preferred Skills & Qualifications

 - Hands-on experience with ML workloads including LLM and/or multimodal training or inference.

 - Deep familiarity with hardware architecture, performance optimizations, compilers, and ML frameworks.

 - Experience designing test strategies for distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and security validation.

 - Experience with microservices deployment, debugging, and orchestration at scale.

 - Prior experience owning or significantly contributing to a team's quality engineering culture or test infrastructure.

Location

This role follows a hybrid schedule, requiring in-office presence 3 days per week. Fully remote is not an option.

About the Role

Cerebras is building a new generation of disaggregated AI inference systems that combine GPU-accelerated prefill with ultra-fast decode on the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine.

We are hiring a Software Engineer to build and evolve the ML API layer that makes this heterogeneous serving system accessible, reliable, and easy to use. You will work across our inference APIs, model integration layer, request-routing services and Cerebras inference platform to deliver a consistent experience across models and accelerator backends.

This role sits at the intersection of machine learning systems, API design, model serving, and distributed systems. You will enable new model architectures and inference capabilities, define stable user-facing behavior, and ensure that features such as streaming, sampling, tool use, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and model configuration behave correctly and consistently in production.

You will work closely with model enablement, compiler, runtime, cloud infrastructure, product, customer-facing teams, and customers directly. This is a hands-on software engineering role for someone who enjoys turning rapidly evolving ML capabilities into durable, production-quality APIs.

Responsibilities

 - Build production ML inference APIs. Design, implement, and maintain APIs for chat completions, text generation, streaming, model configuration, tool calling, structured outputs, multimodal inputs, and other emerging inference capabilities.

 - Deliver a unified serving experience. Create consistent request and response semantics across GPU prefill, Cerebras decode, and other heterogeneous inference backends.

 - Enable new models and capabilities. Integrate emerging foundation models, tokenizers, prompt formats, sampling methods, attention variants, multimodal inputs, and model-specific features into the serving platform.

 - Own API compatibility and evolution. Maintain compatibility with widely adopted inference interfaces while designing Cerebras-specific extensions. Establish clear versioning, deprecation, validation, and backward compatibility practices.

 - Integrate with model-serving runtimes. Extend and integrate custom inference services with vLLM, PyTorch, Hugging Face libraries, the AMD ROCm stack, and Cerebras runtime components.

 - Support disaggregated inference. Build the control and data paths required to coordinate GPU prefill with Cerebras decode, including request routing, state transfer, error handling, retries, and lifecycle management.

 - Improve serving performance. Optimize streaming behavior, time to first token, request latency, throughput, batching, serialization, tokenization, scheduling, and communication between serving components.

 - Ensure functional and numerical correctness. Build validation systems for tokenization, sampling, logits, generated outputs, precision changes, model upgrades, determinism, and compatibility across serving backends.

 - Strengthen reliability and observability. Define end-to-end service indicators and build structured logging, tracing, metrics, dashboards, health checks, and diagnostic tooling for production inference traffic.

 - Develop testing and qualification infrastructure. Create conformance tests, workload-replay tools, model-validation suites, performance benchmarks, integration tests, and release gates.

 - Improve developer experience. Build intuitive configuration, SDKs, documentation, examples, debugging tools, and self-service workflows for internal developers, customers, and partners.

 - Collaborate across the stack. Partner with compiler, runtime, kernel, cloud, product, and solutions teams to translate model and customer requirements into scalable serving capabilities.

Minimum Qualifications

 - 5+ years of software engineering experience, including substantial individual-contributor ownership of production software or distributed systems.

 - Strong programming ability in Python and Go plus experience developing performance-sensitive or highly concurrent services in C++, Rust, or a similar systems language.

 - Experience building stable APIs with clear validation, error handling, observability, compatibility, and versioning practices. 

 - Experience integrating software across service, framework, runtime, and infrastructure boundaries.

 - Experience designing or maintaining OpenAI-compatible, gRPC, REST, or streaming inference APIs. 

 - Experience with Linux, containers, Kubernetes or comparable orchestration systems, CI/CD, and operating latency-sensitive services in production.

 - Ability to diagnose correctness, reliability, and performance issues across multiple components of a distributed serving system.

 - Strong communication and cross-functional execution skills, with the ability to turn ambiguous model or product requirements into production-quality software.

 - Bachelor's degree in computer science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience modifying or contributing to vLLM, SGLang, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Triton, TensorRT-LLM, or another open-source ML systems project.

 - Experience creating API conformance, model-quality, numerical-comparison, determinism, or performance-regression test systems

 - Experience building SDKs, developer tools, model registries, configuration systems, or self-service ML platforms.

 - Experience with multi-model or multi-tenant inference platforms, including routing, admission control, fairness, quotas, rate limiting, and capacity-aware scheduling

 - Understanding of model-specific tokenization, chat templates, generation configuration, logits processing, stopping criteria, tool calling, structured generation, and constrained decoding.

 - Experience with disaggregated prefill/decode architectures, KV-cache transfer, prefix caching, chunked prefill, memory-aware admission control, or request scheduling.

 - Experience designing, building, or operating production APIs and services for machine learning, large language models, or other data-intensive applications. 

 - Familiarity with reduced-precision inference and quantization formats such as BF16, FP8, FP4, INT8, or INT4.

Who we are
 About Stripe
 About the team
 The Risk team builds trust, an essential ingredient for Stripe’s mission to increase the GDP of the internet. We make it possible for millions of businesses to access and use Stripe’s financial infrastructure while protecting our users, financial partners, and the broader ecosystem from harm.
 Risk sits at the center of our users’ and Stripe’s ability to grow safely. We help legitimate businesses access Stripe’s financial services, provide credit to creditworthy businesses, and increasingly help users manage their own risk. We also prevent fraud and financial crime, manage Stripe’s credit exposure, meet our obligations to regulators and financial partners, and enable Stripe’s product teams to launch and grow products safely. To do this, we set the policies and standards that guide how Stripe manages risk and develop the advanced AI, infrastructure, and product experiences that put them into practice for Stripe and our users.
 At Stripe’s scale—$1.9 trillion in annual payment volume, equivalent to 1.6% of global GDP, processed across millions of businesses—we face risk problems no other company has encountered. The opportunities and complexities are only growing as AI reshapes what is possible, Stripe expands its product suite, regulators raise their expectations, and we support more businesses in more countries.
 What you’ll do
 As a Staff Product Manager on the Risk team, you will lead cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives that fundamentally change how Stripe and our users manage risk. You will identify the most important opportunities that cut across Risk’s infrastructure and products, define solutions to our most ambiguous problems, and drive execution from early technical shaping through delivery and adoption.
 You will operate as a product counterpart to Risk’s senior technical leaders. You will shape infrastructure and product direction across Risk, connect work that would otherwise remain fragmented, and help product teams across Stripe build on Risk’s capabilities. You will remain deeply engaged in the work, helping teams navigate difficult technical and product decisions.
 Responsibilities
 Identify high-leverage problems that cut across teams, turn ambiguity into clear product and technical direction, and establish measurable outcomes.
 Lead major cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives from initial shaping through delivery, adoption, and iteration.
 Lead changes in Risk’s approach to using data and AI to accurately identify and mitigate risk at scale.
 Partner deeply with engineering, data science, and machine learning leaders to shape architecture, data foundations, models, APIs, and product experiences.
 Help product teams across Stripe build on Risk’s capabilities quickly and effectively while guiding Risk teams toward coherent, reusable infrastructure and product decisions.
 Build alignment among teams with different goals and constraints, resolve difficult tradeoffs, and drive progress without relying on formal authority.
 Who you are 
 We’re looking for an exceptional product leader who combines strong technical judgment with product insight, strategic range, and executional rigor. You identify important problems before they become obvious, bring clarity to deeply ambiguous spaces, and mobilize teams around solutions that work across products, organizations, and time horizons. You are deeply curious and stay at the forefront of advances in AI and technology, finding practical ways to apply them to our most challenging problems.
 You move fluently from defining multi-year strategy to driving the details of execution. You build alignment and lead transformational work across teams without direct management authority. You earn trust through the clarity of your thinking, your focus on users, and your hands-on engagement in the work. You raise the ambition and effectiveness of the teams and product managers around you without needing to manage them.
 Minimum requirements
 A track record of identifying and delivering high-impact, transformational product or technical initiatives that span multiple teams and organizations.
 Demonstrated ability to bring clarity to deeply ambiguous problems, set a compelling direction, and drive work through execution and adoption.
 Strong technical judgment across data, machine learning, AI, APIs, platforms, and system architecture.
 Experience partnering deeply with senior engineering, data science, and product leaders to shape both technical direction and product strategy.
 Strong product judgment across foundational infrastructure and user-facing experiences, with a focus on building capabilities that solve real user problems.
 Deep quantitative fluency and the ability to use data and causal reasoning to understand problems, evaluate tradeoffs, and measure outcomes.
 Proven ability to influence senior leaders, build alignment across organizational boundaries, and drive execution without direct management authority.
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate compelling strategies, influence technical and executive audiences, and make complex topics clear.
 High agency, intellectual honesty, curiosity, and a low-ego, hands-on working style.
 Preferred qualifications 
 An engineering background, preferably with a focus on machine learning.
 Experience applying AI and machine learning to complex, high-stakes problems at scale.
 Experience with fraud, credit, payments, financial services, trust and safety, or another domain involving complex decisions and asymmetric consequences.
 Experience working with globally distributed teams.

 Manulife is seeking an experienced Senior Manager, Cyber Security Risk Oversight to join Global Information Risk Management, an independent Second Line of Defense function. Reporting to the Director, Cyber Security Risk Oversight – Global Risk, you will lead assigned reviews and assessments, challenge how Line 1 identifies, manages, measures and reports cyber security and technology risk, and turn findings into decision-useful insights for senior leaders and governance forums.

Line 1 remains accountable for identifying, managing and remediating cyber security and technology risk.

 Independent Oversight and Effective Challenge
 Conduct risk-based Line 2 oversight across assigned cyber security and technology risk domains, applying judgment to focus deeper review on higher-risk areas.
 Challenge Line 1 risk assessments, control design and documentation, and risk conclusions.
 Challenge exceptions, issues and remediation plans for adequacy, accountability, timeliness and sustainability, and independently assess closure evidence, escalating material delays or concerns.

 Form independent, evidence-based conclusions and escalate material weaknesses to the Director and relevant governance forums.

 Assess risk across cyber security and technology domains such as identity and access management, cloud security, data protection, network and infrastructure security, application security, vulnerability management, security operations and incident response, technology resilience, third-party technology risk and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.
 Evaluate alignment with risk appetite, internal policies and standards, industry frameworks and regulatory expectations.
 Monitor threat and regulatory developments and reflect emerging risks in assessments.
 Advise project teams on cyber security and technology risk early in the lifecycle, leaving design and control decisions with Line 1.
 Metrics and Risk Measurement Oversight

 Assess metric definitions, data quality, thresholds, trends and completeness to determine whether reporting gives a reliable view of risk.
 Contribute to enhancing Line 2 cyber security and technology risk measurement and reporting.
 Governance, Reporting and Risk Insights

 Contribute analysis to senior-management and Board-level cyber security materials and formal risk positions.
 Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews and other assurance requests with Line 2 perspectives and evidence on assigned cyber security matters.
 Translate technical information into plain business and risk language.
 Facilitate assigned governance routines and follow up on agreed actions.
 Oversight Methodology and Continuous Improvement

 Coordinate with other Line 2 oversight teams to promote consistent risk interpretation and avoid duplication.
 Bring senior perspective to complex or cross-domain matters raised through Information Risk Officer reviews.

In 1967, John Shepherd-Barron reached his bank minutes after closing and could not get at his own money. In the bath that evening, he thought of a chocolate bar dispenser and swapped the chocolate for cash. On 27 June, outside a Barclays branch on Enfield High Street, an actor named Reg Varney drew £10 from the world's first cash machine. It took a four-digit code (originally six, until his wife told him nobody remembers six). The bank's hours had stopped being the customer's problem.
 Nearly sixty years later, the bar has moved, but the test hasn't: a personal financial product is judged on whether it fits the life of the person using it. People do not read documentation, forgive a confusing screen, or care how the ledger works. They want one place that makes sense of everything — spending, saving, planning, investing — and that anticipates rather than reports: where they stand, what deserves attention, what to do next. Mercury is building personal banking* to that standard.
 Personal Banking is how Mercury earns a place in someone's financial life. We're looking for a Head of Product to own it end-to-end: setting product strategy, leading a team of product managers, driving growth and engagement, and owning business performance.
 Key responsibilities:
 Build a personal banking experience so good that people tell their friends and colleagues about it
 Own the metrics, product strategy and the propositions we take to our customers, covering personal money management, banking, savings, investments, money movement, and in the future, lending
 Set the craft bar: sweat the details — copy, latency, empty states — that decide whether a consumer product feels inevitable rather than adequate
 Drive the use of AI in products where it makes the experience meaningfully better
 Build and scale the org: recruit and lead a high-performing PM team, instill strong build discipline, develop future leaders, and set a cadence and culture that drives pace and quality
 Grow the business: own acquisition, activation, retention, and the loops that compound, including how personal banking connects to the businesses Mercury already serves
 Make reliability and trust product features: own uptime, correctness, latency, and support outcomes, and be measured on them
 Align the ecosystem: bring product, engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, legal, marketing, support, and partners behind one cohesive strategy
 Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:
 A consumer product leader with taste: you have built products millions of people chose to use, and can point to the decisions that made them work
 You have shipped AI-led products to real consumers and have opinions about what AI makes possible and where it fails
 An exceptionally high bar for craft, and a customer-centered, data-driven, and experimentation-oriented approach
 10+ years building consumer products, including time owning a product's growth and economics, not only its roadmap
 5+ years leading product managers: hiring, coaching, org design, and performance management
 Experience launching and scaling 0-1 products, alongside operating a large product with real customers on it
 Exceptional cross-functional leadership across engineering, design, data, risk, compliance, and partners
 Nice to have: banking, payments, or fintech experience. We can teach you the rails; we cannot teach product judgment

Core Responsibilities: Enterprise FP&A Forecasting and Capital Planning 
 Lead components of the annual budget, periodic forecasts, and longer-term strategic planning process, coordinating assumptions and inputs across business and functional partners.

 Lead the development and maintenance of the Bank’s capital forecast, including forecast capital ratios, capital generation and consumption, and the impact of business growth and management actions. 
 Lead the forecasting and analysis of RWA, partnering with Risk, Treasury, and business teams to understand underlying balance sheets and risk-weight drivers. 
 Lead FP&A activities supporting the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP) and enterprise stress testing, including assessment of financial and capital impacts under alternative scenarios. 
 Review and challenge business, financial, and capital assumptions and forecast outputs through reasonableness checks, back-testing, variance analysis, and comparison to actual performance.

 Partner with Treasury, Risk, Accounting, and business teams to align key assumptions and maintain a coherent enterprise financial and capital outlook.

 Develop analysis supporting enterprise planning, resource allocation, capital allocation, and balance sheet management decisions. 
 Evaluate potential business, management, and capital actions through scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis. 
 Translate detailed financial and capital analysis into clear, concise insights for senior management and Board-level reporting.

 Provide ad hoc financial and strategic analysis as required by senior and executive management. 
 Forecasting, Modelling and Process Enhancement

 Identify opportunities to improve forecast accuracy, controls, validation, efficiency, and data integration. 
 Develop appropriate modelling methodologies for new products, businesses, and capital requirements.

 Support automation of capital and financial planning processes, including continued integration with enterprise forecasting tools. 
 Establish appropriate controls and review processes for key capital planning deliverables. 
 Leadership and Stakeholder Coordination

 Build trusted relationships across FP&A, Treasury, Risk, Accounting, and the business to support an integrated approach to capital planning. 
 Challenge assumptions constructively and communicate capital considerations to stakeholders with varying levels of financial and technical expertise .

 Manulife's GWAM Operations manages the Company’s General Account on-balance sheet assets and assets for institutional clients and investment funds in key markets around the world.  It provides investment management services to affiliates’ retail clients through product offerings of Manulife and John Hancock.  It manages a broad range of investments including public and private bonds, public and private equities, mortgages, real estate, oil and gas, infrastructure, timberland, farmland and asset allocation strategies.  It has a physical presence in key international financial centers, including Canada, the United States, Hong Kong, Japan, the United Kingdom, Australia and South East Asia. 
 Role Overview: 
 The Securities and Mortgage Accounting team plays a key role in ensuring accurate, consistent and timely accounting for securities within the General Account, under multiple accounting bases.
 Reporting to the Director, Securities and Mortgage Accounting, the Senior Financial Analyst is a key member of the Securities and Mortgage Accounting team. This position is responsible for the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of accounting transactions in the AABOR system (the administration and accounting book of record for securities). The incumbent will assist the Director in providing sound advice to business partners on accounting treatments and procedures in order to maintain the integrity of the AABOR and General Ledger systems.
 Position Responsibilities: 
 Production: 
 Ensure accounting treatment for securities is in line with regulatory requirements across multiple accounting bases (e.g., IFRS, USGAAP, Statutory, and Tax).
 Responsible for the accuracy and timeliness of accounting results for the month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes.
 Responsible for and oversight of key reconciliations between SCD and INFOR, Enterprise and INFOR, and analytics.
 Assist with day-to-day operational functions related to cash/suspense, securities transfers, corporate actions, impairments, CTA process, and other general inquiries.
 Participate in special projects and initiatives.
 Collaborate with various business partners such as Trade Operations, Cash Management and Custody Services, Investment Accounting and Reporting, Asset Liability Management, Investment Systems, and Corporate Controllers for day-to-day activities as well as special transactions/projects.
 Service Quality and Risk Management: 
 Work with Controls Center of Excellence (COE) and Internal and External Auditors for SOX walkthroughs, detailed testing, and annual audits. Ensure requests are addressed in a timely manner.
 Demonstrate controls and maintain properly documented policies and procedures.
 Required Qualifications: 
 University degree required in business, accounting, or finance.
 Attained or actively pursuing a professional accounting designation (CPA/CA/CMA/CGA).
 3–5 years of experience in the investment/insurance industry, preferably within a securities accounting area.
 Attention to detail. Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
 Solid organizational skills, including the ability to effectively plan, prioritize multiple tasks, and meet tight deadlines.
 Ability to build and maintain strong relationships and excellent communication skills.
 Comfortable with challenging the status quo. Flexible and change-oriented attitude that embraces new ideas and ways of working.
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Strong knowledge of IFRS/USGAAP/NAIC in relation to investment accounting and reporting would be ideal.
 Expert user of Microsoft Access and Excel. Experience with VBA Macros will be an asset.
 Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset. If the successful candidate is in Québec, proficiency in both languages will be required to support clients from various provinces outside of Quebec.

Senior Machine Learning Engineer, AI & Agentic Systems
 The Opportunity
 Ready to build AI solutions that move beyond experimentation and deliver real business impact?
 Join the John Hancock AI team and help shape the next generation of intelligent solutions across our U.S. Insurance business. You’ll work on high-impact opportunities spanning sales and marketing, financial operations, insurance servicing, claims, and advisor and customer experiences.
 As part of a global community of 260+ data scientists across John Hancock and Manulife , you’ll collaborate with AI, engineering, product, architecture, operations, risk, and business leaders while helping transform how we use AI across the organization.
 We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer who can bridge the gap between innovative AI concepts and secure, scalable production solutions. You’ll have the opportunity to build everything from traditional machine learning and deep learning models to LLM-powered applications and agentic AI systems , while helping establish the engineering standards and governance needed to use AI responsibly in a regulated environment.
 If you enjoy solving complex problems, building production-grade AI systems, and influencing how emerging technologies are adopted at scale, this could be the opportunity for you.
 What You’ll Do
 Build production AI: Design, develop, deploy, and operationalize machine learning, deep learning, NLP, and LLM-based solutions that solve meaningful business problems.
 Develop agentic AI systems: Create production-grade AI agents using retrieval, orchestration, structured tool use, event-driven integrations, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
 Scale intelligent automation: Lead initiatives that expand agentic AI and automation across operations, marketing, back-office functions, and customer and advisor journeys.
 Create reusable AI capabilities: Develop reference architectures, platform capabilities, patterns, tools, and integrations that enable teams to build AI solutions securely and efficiently.
 Establish AI engineering standards: Help define practices for agent identity and access, data protection, tool use, evaluation, auditability, human oversight, release controls, and lifecycle management.
 Strengthen AI evaluation and observability: Establish approaches for measuring quality, safety, reliability, latency, cost, adoption, task completion, and business value.
 Partner across the business: Work closely with engineering, architecture, product, operations, risk, security, compliance, and business teams to identify and deliver high-value AI opportunities.
 Influence technology direction: Evaluate AI models, frameworks, platforms, and vendors, and provide recommendations based on security, interoperability, performance, cost, and strategic fit.
 Lead and mentor: Provide technical leadership to engineers through mentoring, workshops, demonstrations, architecture reviews, documentation, and engineering best practices.
 What You Bring
 5+ years of software engineering, machine learning engineering, or related experience , including a demonstrated track record of deploying AI solutions into production.
 Strong software engineering experience building distributed applications, APIs, event-driven systems, and cloud-native services .
 Hands-on programming experience with technologies such as Python, Java, .NET, Node.js, React, and SQL .
 Experience developing AI-enabled applications, LLM solutions, AI agents, or workflow automation , including retrieval, tool calling, orchestration, and structured outputs.
 Experience with Azure AI services, Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure AI Search, Databricks, and GitHub Actions .
 Strong understanding of CI/CD, automated testing, observability, security, reliability, and production readiness .
 Knowledge of AI evaluation, guardrails, privacy, security, Responsible AI, human oversight, and auditability, particularly in regulated environments.
 Experience with Databricks, data modeling, and data-product development .
 Experience with distributed computing technologies such as Spark or Hadoop , cloud platforms including Azure, AWS, or GCP , and container technologies including Docker and Kubernetes .
 Ability to translate business challenges into technical solutions, roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes.
 Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to lead technical workshops, design reviews, training sessions, and discussions with senior stakeholders.
 Experience mentoring engineers and improving engineering practices across teams.
 Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Engineering, Computer Science, or another quantitative or technical discipline.
 What Will Help You Stand Out
 Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an asset:
 Agent orchestration frameworks and integration standards such as LangGraph, Microsoft Agent Framework, Model Context Protocol (MCP), or Agent2Agent (A2A) .
 LLMOps or AgentOps , including prompt and model versioning, automated evaluation, evaluation datasets, quality gates, tracing, telemetry, rollout strategies, and regression testing.
 AI governance and Responsible AI practices within regulated environments.
 AI or workflow automation within financial services, insurance, financial operations, or regulated customer experiences .
 Measuring the impact of AI platforms through adoption, engineering productivity, operational efficiency, quality, risk reduction, or customer outcomes.
 NLP solutions such as document classification, entity extraction, and entity relationship extraction .
 Building and applying knowledge graphs .
 Computer vision experience.
 What Motivates You
 You’re someone who:
 Puts customers at the center of the solutions you build.
 Thinks big and stays curious about what emerging AI technologies can make possible.
 Enjoys collaborating across disciplines to turn ideas into working solutions.
 Takes ownership and focuses on outcomes that matter.
 Acts with integrity and is comfortable raising risks or challenging assumptions.
 Enjoys sharing knowledge, mentoring others, and contributing to an inclusive engineering culture.
 Build What’s Next
 John Hancock and Manulife are transforming financial services to make decisions easier and experiences simpler for our customers. This role gives you the opportunity to be part of that transformation while working at the intersection of machine learning, generative AI, agentic systems, cloud engineering, and Responsible AI .
 You won’t just experiment with emerging AI technology. You’ll help turn it into secure, scalable solutions that deliver measurable value.

The Role
 At Treewalk, you'll run the day-to-day finance engine for the Indigenous governments, organizations and businesses we serve: clean books, a disciplined month-end close, timely funder reporting and year-end files that sail through audit. You'll own a portfolio of clients, acting as their fractional controller. Some will lean on you to keep operations running smoothly month to month; others will need you to get a backlog cleaned up and audit-ready. Either way, every file is yours to run.
 If you've managed controllership or audit-prep engagements at a small- to mid-size firm, or run finance operations inside a First Nation, Tribal Council or Indigenous organization, and you're ready for high-impact work, tangible ownership and genuine balance, then we would love to hear from you.
 •         Run a disciplined close – Lead month-end and year-end close across your portfolio: reconciliations, accruals, deferred revenue, capital assets and journal entries, on time and review-ready.
 •         Keep operations humming – Oversee AP, AR, payroll and cash management processes, and step in hands-on when a client needs a fractional controller's precision and speed.
 •         Make audits painless – Build year-end audit files and lead schedules, prep airtight support, clear PBC lists and quarterback conversations with external auditors so leadership can sleep at night.
 •         Get the hard files back on track – Clean up backlogs and prior-year issues, so clients go from catch-up mode to a clean, audit-ready position.
 •         Run the engine of multi-entity groups – Keep the books straight across Nations' governments, economic development corporations, limited partnerships, trusts and societies, including intercompany and fund accounting.
 •         Keep funding on track – Track funding by program, manage deferred and restricted funds, and prepare reporting for ISC, CIRNAC, FNHA and other funders.
 •         Build strong controls – Design practical processes, internal controls and financial policies that hold up to auditor and funder scrutiny.
 •         Grow the team – Coach and review the work of accountants, bookkeepers and CPA students, and build checklists and templates that scale across clients.
 Result: clients see you as the calm, trusted voice who keeps their books clean, their funders satisfied and their audits uneventful, while you build deep, meaningful expertise without the grind of traditional public practice. 
 Our ideal candidate...
 •         CPA designation required.
 •         Significant experience in controllership, month-end close and year-end audit preparation, ideally with Indigenous governments, organizations or not-for-profits.
 •         Strong working knowledge of PSAS / ASNPO, fund accounting and funding agreement reporting.
 •         Experience leading engagements and supervising staff.
 •         A respectful, relationship-based approach and an understanding of Indigenous histories, governance and the impacts of colonization.
 •         After the base experience requirements are met, we hire first and foremost strong analytical thinkers and problem solvers.
 Please mention these bonus skills if you have them
 •         Audit experience at a firm serving First Nations or public-sector clients
 •         Cloud accounting and payroll systems (e.g., QuickBooks Online, Sage, Xero)
 •         FMB Financial Administration Law or certification experience
 •         Lived experience as a First Nations, Métis or Inuit person, or connection to Indigenous communities
 Why Treewalk Feels Different
 Who We Are
 Treewalk is Vancouver-born and scaling nationwide. Our Indigenous Services group runs the finance operations of Nations and Indigenous organizations and gets them audit-ready, so leadership can focus on their community's goals while we keep the numbers strong.
 •         Relationships first – We earn trust over the long term and work in a way that respects each community's priorities and protocols.
 •         Training ground for tomorrow's leaders – Whether you're two years post-designation or a seasoned finance lead, Treewalk is where accountants level up.
 The Values That Power Us
 Mastery: We hunt knowledge relentlessly and build expertise into every engagement.
 Annual Salary - $110,000

 Nous fabriquons et fournissons des médicaments et des vaccins fiables et de haute qualité afin de répondre aux besoins des patients et de soutenir notre performance. 
 Notre réseau mondial de production met la science, la technologie et les talents au service des patients.  À titre de Technicien de production, vous participez aux différentes étapes du procédé de fabrication, préparez les solutions nécessaires à la production et aux analyses et exécutez des activités de validation.

 ·     Manipuler les équipements de production et de laboratoire, documenter les étapes en temps réel, prélever des échantillons de contrôle et diluer ou mélanger les substances et les vaccins en préservant leur intégrité et leur stérilité.

We are looking for a Director of Supply Chain Management to build and lead the operating infrastructure required to bring our products to market, scale them globally, and support them throughout their lifecycle. This role sits within the Supply Chain organization and reports to the Sr. Director, Operations & Strategic Partnerships. This role has high exposure to CEO level decisions and engagement and demonstrated leadership experience is a requirement.
 This is a builder role within the Supply Chain. You will own the Supply Chain deliverables covering our cross functional go to market and customer engagement. This includes driving product certifications and market readiness, enhancing RMA and customer satisfaction processes, as well as driving our Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Your job is to establish clear ownership, build scalable processes, develop the team, and create the operating mechanisms required to support a rapidly growing hardware business, working in close partnership with the other functions needed to achieve these goals.
 We are not looking for someone to administer existing processes. We are looking for someone who sees ambiguity, creates structure, drives decisions, and most importantly takes end-to-end ownership. Your mandate is simple: build it, own it, and scale it.
 This role is hybrid, based out of Toronto, ON; Austin, TX; or Santa Clara, CA. 
 Who You Are 
 A builder who is comfortable entering an environment where processes and ownership are not fully defined, then turning ambiguity into a clear operating model and an executable plan.
 An experienced hardware and supply chain operator who understands how Engineering, Product, Sales, Manufacturing, Quality, Finance, Legal, and customer teams connect across the product lifecycle.
 A cross-functional leader who can align senior stakeholders, establish decision rights, and drive accountability without waiting for someone else to define ownership.
 A data-driven and analytically rigorous decision-maker who can make sound judgments with incomplete information and maintain urgency through execution.
 A people leader who develops strong teams, builds subject matter expertise, and creates a culture of ownership, transparency, and continuous improvement.
 What We Need 
 Drive cross-functional processes and own Supply Chain deliverables for global product certification and market readiness, including certification roadmaps across products and countries, clear readiness gates, coordination with Engineering, Product, Legal, manufacturing partners, test labs, and regulatory bodies, and early mitigation of risks that could affect customer commitments or launches.
 Own and mature the company’s S&OP process by connecting customer demand, Sales forecasts, supply, manufacturing capacity, inventory, and financial objectives into a disciplined operating cadence and trusted view for executive decision-making.
 Build and own the end-to-end global RMA and customer operations model within Supply Chain, covering intake, triage, replacement, repair, warranty management, disposition, customer communication, service levels, escalation paths, and performance metrics, in partnership with Customer, Quality, and Engineering teams.
 Establish the processes, systems, KPIs, dashboards, governance, and operating mechanisms required to scale, including measures for forecast accuracy, supply performance, inventory health, backlog, certification readiness, RMA performance, and execution against plan.
 Lead cross-functional execution with Sales, Product, Engineering, Quality, Finance, Manufacturing, test labs, regulatory bodies, and customer teams. Establish clear decision rights, simplify complex workflows, identify gaps before they become business problems, and drive shared decisions through to completion while retaining Supply Chain ownership of the deliverables.
 What You Will Learn 
 Gain broad exposure to the full operating model of a rapidly growing hardware and semiconductor business, from product development and global market readiness through supply planning, manufacturing, delivery, and customer support.
 Build expertise in integrating Supply Chain-owned certification deliverables, S&OP, RMA, and customer operations into one scalable product lifecycle operating system.
 Develop the leadership and operating mechanisms required to turn cross-functional complexity into clear ownership, timely decisions, and measurable execution.
 See directly how operational decisions influence product launch timing, customer commitments, product quality, inventory, revenue, and the company’s ability to scale globally.
 Create the foundation for a supply chain management organization that grows with Tenstorrent’s products, markets, customers, and operational complexity.
 Compensation for all engineers at Tenstorrent ranges from $100k - $500k including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.

Functionally reports to Extrusion Team Lead. Responsible for optimally operating the press, process equipment, handling equipment and die setup in a safe and efficient manner. Responsible for following Company policies and procedures by ensuring a safe working environment is maintained at all times.  We believe that every Employee is responsible to act safely and to model good safety practices.
 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 The duties and responsibilities of the Press Operator are detailed below, but not limited to the following:
 Efficiently operate the extrusion press while maintaining good quality that meets Almag’s quality standards. 
 Keep track of equipment performance and ensure press is well tuned, and temperatures are being properly managed from billet oven to press exit temperatures.
 Responsible for monitoring runout efficiency such as length, speed, and finish.
 Reference work orders to ensure press is running at the optimal speeds to maximize productivity.
 Ensure billet zone temperatures are setup, monitored and maintained throughout the runs. Mark extrusions accordingly if temperatures do not meet requirements.
 Die management - Ensure all necessary tooling is available at the beginning and throughout shift.
 Load dies into press and ensure presses are not waiting for die changes. Importance must be given to ensure dies are not loaded too early or too late.
 Ensure die temperatures are maintained when dies are loaded and removed from the ovens.
 Responsible for communicating directly with the team leads/maintenance team if any mechanical breakdowns or issues are encountered.
 Ensure proper billets/logs are in the ovens and monitor the supply to keep press going.
 Ensure average speeds are followed based on information contained on work orders. If deviations occur, ensure note is made in EPICS and Team Lead is notified.
 Responsible for EPICS entries for billet lengths, cut offs, cut sizes, etc., and highlight any special notes and instructions that the team needs to focus on. 
 Responsible for entering all downtime, die fails, quality issues, and schedule adherence notes in EPICS.
 Responsible for checking notes in EPICS and viewing drawings throughout the shift to ensure work orders are followed correctly.
 Responsible for checking the run out on the second billet produced. Report to Team Lead if billet length scheduled is inappropriate and have it changed to improve yield.
 Ensure sufficient spacing is kept between extrusion pieces on the cooling table to make sure proper cooling is maintained.
 Responsible for ensuring the extrusion is correctly fed into puller jaws. Notify maintenance/team lead if any issues occur.
 Ensure exit/runout temperatures are monitored and maintained throughout the run. 
 Maintain quality checks at front end of press during operation and continuously throughout the shift.
 Press samples must be properly labelled and kept together for traceability
 Ensure samples are taken after the first billet and verify dimensions and surface finish according to drawings in EPICS.
 Ensure all billets and alloys used are accounted for in EPICS and documented accurately.
 Check finish and dimensions on extrusions at the required frequency.
 Complete press Ascona scans as required.
 Must have knowledge and ability to operate all equipment at saw and stretcher.
 Other duties as assigned. 
 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 
 Education/Experience 
 High school Diploma with some technical background and mechanical aptitude.
 Extrusion experience is an asset.
 Technical Skills/Competence 
 1-2 years’ experience in an industrial environment.
 Knowledge of machinery and ability to read drawings is an asset. Willing to train.  
 Must be willing and able to train and develop as a saw operator / inspector, stretcher operator and die preparation operator as understating these jobs and their impact is critical to developing as a competent press operator.
 Basic computer skills including MS Windows is required. Other MS software is an asset. 
 Understanding of measurements, tolerances, basic geometry, and numeracy comprehension.
 Ability to lift up-to 50lbs independently, and ability to lift up-to 100lbs in collaboration with a team member.
 Familiarity with extrusion software such as EPICS is an asset.

 Health & Dental 
 Health Care Spending Account
 Education Assistance Program

 Company Events 
 Floater Days 
 Paid Holidays 
 Shift Premiums
 Annual safety footwear reimbursement program

ABOUT REMARCABLE

Remarcable is building the digital operating system for contractors and distributors—solving critical procurement, supply chain, and financial workflow pain points that have plagued the construction industry for decades. With proven product-market fit, backing from Insight Partners, and a rapidly scaling business, we’re looking for a Product Manager who is excited to lead and scale our core Procure-to-Pay (P2P) and accounting integration ecosystem.

This is not a "just keep the roadmap moving" type of role. You’ll be a strategic owner, systems thinker, and technical product leader who bridges the gap between field procurement and back-office financial systems. Working closely with engineering, product, integrations, and go-to-market teams, you will architect and drive the workflows that automate purchase orders, invoice matching, job costing, and complex ERP synchronization at scale.

If you thrive at the intersection of technical architecture, financial/accounting logic, and customer strategy—and you want your work to make a profound, visible difference in a multi-billion-dollar market—this role is for you.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the Product Strategy & Lifecycle: Drive the vision, roadmap, and execution for our procurement, accounts payable, and accounting integration domains from concept to launch.

 - Master Complex Financial Logic: Dive deep into sophisticated accounting systems—including 3-way matching (PO, receiving slip, and invoice), job cost tracking, general ledger (GL) routing, and cost code mapping.

 - Lead ERP Integration Initiatives: Collaborate closely with engineering pods and integration specialists to translate intricate enterprise ERP data structures and accounting rules into bulletproof, seamless software features.

 - Drive Agile Execution & Culture: Lead agile ceremonies, backlog prioritization, and cross-functional planning to ensure predictable, high-leverage software delivery.

 - Translate Requirements into Scale: Synthesize complex back-office workflows and user feedback into clear, executable specs and scalable system architectures.

 - Partner on Technical Trade-Offs: Bring strong technical fluency to architectural discussions, evaluating data schemas, API integrations, performance constraints, and technical debt.

 - Define Business Impact: Establish, track, and optimize key product metrics (KPIs) centered on feature adoption, financial data accuracy, and operational time-savings.

 - Leverage AI & Modern Workflows: Champion the use of AI tools and automated workflows to accelerate product discovery, data validation, and user documentation.

WHO YOU ARE

 - 4+ years of Product Management experience in a B2B SaaS environment, with a strong focus on data-heavy, workflow, fintech, or enterprise integration products.

 - Technical Background: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Business Technology Management, or a related quantitative field.

 - Domain Fluency: Deep familiarity with foundational accounting workflows, such as Accounts Payable (AP), Procure-to-Pay (P2P), purchase orders, invoice automation, or construction job costing.

 - Systems-First Mindset: Highly analytical; deeply comfortable mapping data across systems, designing relational data models, and troubleshooting API exchanges.

 - Exceptional Communicator: Able to distill complex technical architecture and financial logic into clear, concise direction for developers, executives, and users alike.

 - Proven Execution Leader: Track record of driving cross-functional product initiatives independently and thriving in a fast-paced, high-ambiguity startup environment.

NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Hands-on experience with construction accounting platforms or mid-market/enterprise ERPs (e.g., Sage 100/300, QuickBooks Enterprise, NetSuite, Viewpoint/Vista, or Acumatica).

 - Proficiency with SQL for data analysis, query writing, and log investigation.

 - Direct experience shipping features leveraging OCR invoice capture, automated rule engines, or embedded AI capabilities.

WHY JOIN REMARCABLE?

We’re a Series A SaaS company backed by Insight Partners, scaling fast with a mission to transform construction operations. Our platform has already processed billions in material purchases, and we’re just getting started.

At Remarcable, you’ll:

 - Own High-Impact Scope: Your products will directly automate and optimize financial workflows for major contractors and distributors across North America.

 - High Ownership & Autonomy: Work in a lean, elite team where strategic decisions are made fast and execution matters.

 - Tackle Massive Inefficiencies: Build software that modernizes one of the largest, least digitized industries in the world.

OUR MISSION

To advance technology adoption in the construction industry by delivering efficiency, visibility, and communication at scale.

Full-time | Vancouver

 - Own the day-to-day operations of client research studies. Keep track of what's coming in, what's in progress, and what needs attention.

 - Help clients turn their research questions into well-designed studies. You'll write and review study guides, configure studies in our platform, set up targeting and quotas, and launch them to Pogo users.

 - Work directly with clients to keep them updated on their studies, answer questions, troubleshoot issues, and manage expectations.

 - Work closely with our GTM and Product teams to help coordinate requests, share client feedback, and identify opportunities to improve our product.

 - Help us build better processes. We're growing quickly, and a lot of our workflows are still being figured out. You'll help us improve our tools, templates, QA processes, and AI-powered workflows so we can scale.

 - You likely have 2–4 years of experience in market research, ideally at a research agency, panel provider, or in-house consumer insights team.

 - You're comfortable managing a lot of studies at once. You can stay organized, keep track of the details, and prioritize when everything feels urgent.

 - You're detail-oriented, catching issues with survey design, logic, and data quality before they become problems.

 - You're proactive, resourceful, and comfortable figuring things out independently.

 - You thrive in fast-paced environments and can adapt quickly as priorities change.

 - You're systems-minded, always looking for ways to improve processes, automate repetitive work, and make things more efficient.

 - You'll work with some of the world's largest consumer brands, helping them make important strategic decisions through consumer research.

The team owns the systems between a customer and the underlying AI infrastructure, including identity, deployments, metering, billing, security, privacy, and confidential computing. We are strengthening these systems as Model Vault grows, with the goal of scaling to millions of users and supporting some of the world’s most demanding enterprise workloads.

 - Build highly reliable control-plane services for provisioning, configuring, scaling, and operating model deployments across clouds and hardware platforms.

 - Design APIs and distributed systems with strong guarantees around correctness, consistency, isolation, failure recovery, idempotency, and observability.

 - Build security and privacy into the platform architecture, including tenant isolation, least-privilege access, auditability, secrets management, encryption, and confidential computing boundaries.

 - Solve complex problems that span backend systems, cloud infrastructure, security, and AI inference, where conventional SaaS patterns are often not enough.

ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS
 New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.
We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.
 ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY
 The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities. 
 This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.
 The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Fundraising Strategy & Prioritization (50%) 
 Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
 Synthesize funder conversations, proposal outcomes, market signals and intelligence generated across the organization into clear fundraising priorities
 Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
 Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
 Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
 Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.
 Team Coordination & Enablement (35%) 
 Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
 Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
 Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
 Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
 Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
 Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
 Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
 Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
 Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
 Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.
 Systems, Data & Reporting (15%) 
 Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
 Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
 Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
 Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.
 Ensure fundraising protocols and internal as well as external reporting are completed on time and to consistent quality standards
 SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS
 Success in this role will mean building a more coordinated, strategic, and effective global development function. By the end of the first 6–12 months, the Director will have:
 Established clear visibility into NEX's global fundraising pipeline, priorities, risks, and opportunities, with leadership able to make decisions based on reliable, current information.
 Built a strong operating rhythm across the global platform-level development team, with clear ownership, effective collaboration, and team members' skills deployed against the highest-priority fundraising opportunities.
 Improved coordination across platform, country, and program teams so that high-value proposals are prioritized appropriately, developed collaboratively, and submitted on time and at a consistently high quality.
 Established consistent CRM and pipeline management practices across the development function, with data being used to inform strategy, prioritization, and reporting.
 Created a well-organized, accessible library of standardized fundraising collateral and tools that enables fundraisers and country teams to move more quickly and consistently.
 Established effective feedback loops between funder and country-level intelligence, fundraising performance, and the organization's overall development strategy.
 Professional Experience 
 8+ years of experience across nonprofit fundraising/development, development strategy and/or development operations, including at least 5 years working directly within nonprofit or philanthropic fundraising. Candidates must demonstrate a deep practical understanding of the fundraising cycle, funder decision-making, proposal development and stewardship.
 Strong track record leading the development of complex philanthropic/grant proposals, ideally involving multiple programmes, geographies or internal stakeholders.
 Demonstrated experience turning frontline or field-level input into strategy and prioritization. 
 Demonstrated people-management experience, including coaching, performance management, setting priorities and allocating team capacity. Experience leading a distributed team is strongly preferred.
 Experience operating in a global or matrix organisation, with demonstrated ability to influence and coordinate country leaders, programme teams and other stakeholders who do not report directly to them.
 Comfortable using CRM and pipeline data to support fundraising decisions, forecasting and team management.
 Familiarity with the climate, clean energy, or entrepreneurship support landscape is a strong plus.
 Experience conducting dedicated funder-market or landscape research is advantageous.
 Personal Attributes 
 Structured, analytical thinker who is comfortable synthesizing messy, qualitative field input into clear recommendations.
 High level of adaptability in an environment with evolving team structures and workflows, with a genuine comfort operating in ambiguity - this means being a self-starter and embodying a growth mindset.
 High emotional intelligence — able to lead and support a development team well, build trust with country leads across diverse cultural contexts, and approach unfamiliar markets and norms with genuine curiosity and cultural sensitivity.
 Exceptional written communication skills — able to distill complex, multi-market fundraising intelligence into concise strategy and proposals.
 Strong project management skills; able to run a coordination function across concurrent proposals, deadlines, and stakeholders.
 Comfortable being an internal partner and "connective tissue" role rather than the primary external face of fundraising.
 Ability to work with a global team across time zones, with periodic travel for internal team meetings and relevant conferences/convenings.
 Proficiency in database/CRM management, Google Workspace, and Slack.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Foundational knowledge of global clean energy and climate change solutions and ecosystems and willingness to engage in in-depth self-learning on any gaps.
 Experience building or adding structure to a development operations function from an earlier, more informal stage.
 Due to the global nature of the organization and team, some meetings will take place outside of regular work hours.
 BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION
 This is a full-time remote position. Relocation assistance is not available for this role and compensation is competitive for the market the candidate is based in. Applicable benefits such as medical, dental, vision, paid time off, paid holidays and insurance will depend on the location of the selected candidate.

New Energy Nexus hires and promotes individuals on the basis of their qualifications for the job to be filled. We strongly encourage diverse applicants to apply.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based and is not an employment relationship.
 What this opportunity involves 
 We're looking for contributors to share their own medical lab report. You add the original files, and details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, and contact details, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. You also check the redacted preview before you submit. The lab's name and address, the test names, and the results stay in the report. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. The files help improve AI systems that read and understand medical documents. In this project, contributors may:
 Add the PDF file of their own lab report, for example blood test results;
 Take an iPhone photo of each printed page of the report and a screenshot of each page on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac;
 Check the redacted preview of each page and submit it only if all details that identify them are covered;
 Add one report per task;
 Submit clear files where every page of the report is fully visible.
 If you have your own lab test results and are comfortable sharing them once your personal details are covered, apply to take part in this project.
 What we look for 
 This opportunity is a good fit for people who have their own lab test results and are open to a short-term, project-based collaboration. To take part, contributors will need:
 To be 18 to 65 years old and live in one of these countries: the UK, Canada, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Poland, Portugal, Brazil, Spain, Türkiye, Norway, Indonesia, the UAE, or Israel (no VPN while using Mindrift);
 Their own medical lab report as a PDF file (1 to 10 pages): lab test results only, such as a blood count, blood chemistry, or a urine test;
 A report from a lab in the country where they live, preferably in the local language (reports in English, or in both languages, are also accepted);
 A printed copy of the report, an iPhone (any model) for the photos, and an iPhone, iPad, or Mac for the screenshots.
 This opportunity is not suitable for someone else’s lab report (for example, a family member’s), a translated or edited copy of a report, or other medical documents such as discharge summaries or surgery notes. 
 How it works  
 Apply → Get an email from Mindrift Team (check spam too) → Register on Mindrift → Verify your identity → Sign the project consent form → Add your report's PDF, photos, and screenshots and check the redacted preview → Get paid for each accepted report 
 Privacy
 Taking part is voluntary, and choosing not to take part doesn’t affect your Mindrift account. Before your first task, you read and sign a project consent form. Details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses, as well as doctors' names and signatures, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. Your original files are deleted. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. We never ask you to send your report by email, chat or anywhere outside the Mindrift platform.
 Project time expectations 
 Each lab report is a separate task, and you can add reports whenever it suits you while the project is active. This is a time-limited project, and the number of reports we can accept is not guaranteed. Reports need to meet the listed criteria to be accepted. If a report needs a fix, it comes back to you with the reason. 
 Earnings  
 Paid per accepted report:  $10 for every lab report  (PDF, photos, and screenshots of each page) that passes our quality checks. Earnings are added to your Mindrift balance once the report is accepted. 
 You can withdraw them to your bank account or PayPal via Tipalti, or via Payoneer (minimum $20). Payouts are processed twice a month. Mindrift doesn't deduct any fees, but your payment provider may charge a small transfer fee.

About Flinks 
 The Role
 We're hiring our Senior Data Engineer (Data / ML Platform) to stand up data engineering as a discipline at Flinks . You'll own the data and ML platform that turns models into reliable production services, harden the data models the business runs on and close the seam between our data scientists and the product teams. This is a high-ownership, greenfield-leaning role: much of this foundation is yours to build and own, not inherit.
 If you like being the person who makes data and ML production-grade - pipelines, serving, governance, reliability - and you want broad impact across a company's data, this is built for you.
 What You'll Do
 Own and evolve the data platform - the BigQuery warehouse, dbt transformation layers, Airflow / Cloud Composer orchestration and Pub/Sub ingestion that feed every model and metric.
 Build and operate the ML platform - training pipelines (Kubeflow on Vertex AI), model serving (FastAPI behind Vertex endpoints), CI/CD, containerization and typed contracts. Take operational ownership of model-serving infrastructure so reliability isn't carried by the data scientists alone.
 Harden and standardize the data models the business depends on - improving schemas, fixing data-quality issues and establishing trustworthy source-of-truth feeds.
 Establish data governance and observability - bring data that lives outside the warehouse under proper governance and build operational metrics for products that don't yet have them .
 Standardize how data engineering is done across product lines - patterns, tooling and pipelines other teams can adopt.
 Partner across data science, backend and product on the producer to consumer contract (models produced by data science, consumed/aggregated downstream, surfaced to clients).
 What You'll Work On
 You'll help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' financial intelligence products, supporting everything from transaction enrichment and categorization to risk and payments decisioning.
 Key areas of focus include:
 Building scalable data pipelines that process and transform large volumes of financial data. 
 Designing and maintaining reliable datasets, data models, and feature pipelines used by machine learning and product teams. 
 Improving data quality, observability, and operational metrics across our platform and customer-facing products. 
 Developing cost-efficient, high-performance data services and infrastructure that support real-time and batch workloads. 
 Partnering closely with Data Science, Product, and Engineering teams to enable new capabilities and accelerate product delivery. 
 Contributing to the evolution of our data platform architecture as we continue to scale our products, customers, and machine learning capabilities.
 Our stack
 Python, SQL, Bash 
 Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 
 BigQuery and dbt 
 Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub, and Cloud Functions 
 Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow, and FastAPI 
 Docker, Terraform, and Protocol Buffers 
 Azure DevOps 
 Grafana and GCP Logging 
 You don't need experience with every tool listed above - strong Data Engineering fundamentals and experience building production data platforms matter more than direct experience with our exact stack. SQL is the exception : it's a non-negotiable (see Key Requirements). 
 Why This Role
 Greenfield ownership — help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' next generation of data and machine learning products. 
 High leverage impact — your work enables Data Science, Product, Engineering, and Risk teams to move faster with reliable, trusted data. 
 Real-world scale and complexity — work with large volumes of financial data powering products used by banks, fintechs, and financial institutions across North America. 
 Modern cloud-native environment — build on a modern GCP stack using contemporary data, platform, and machine learning tooling.
 Key Requirements
 Experience: 5+ years of hands-on Data Engineering experience designing, building, and operating production data platforms, pipelines, and warehouse solutions in a cloud environment.
 Data Engineering Expertise: Strong experience with ETL/ELT development, data modeling, schema design, orchestration, data quality, lineage, and warehouse optimization. Experience with BigQuery, dbt, Airflow, or equivalent modern data tooling is highly desirable.
 Technical Foundation: Expert SQL and strong Python skills, with the ability to build scalable, maintainable, and well-tested data solutions that support both operational and analytical workloads.
 Cloud Data Platforms: Experience working with modern cloud-native data ecosystems, including data warehouses, event-driven architectures, distributed processing, and platform observability.
 Operational Excellence: Demonstrated ownership of production systems, including monitoring, reliability, performance tuning, cost optimization, incident response, and ongoing platform improvements.
 Machine Learning Platform Exposure: Experience supporting machine learning workflows, feature pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, or MLOps environments is an asset, but a strong Data Engineering foundation is the primary requirement.
 Collaboration: Ability to partner effectively with Data Science, Product, Engineering, and QA teams to deliver trusted, scalable, and well-governed data solutions.
 Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
 Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in Canada.
 Benefits 
 As part of the total rewards package, Flinks offers:
 Health & Dental coverage as of Day 1
 Flexible Paid Time Off (FTO)
 Remote work environment with frequent in-person gatherings and activities.
 Career development, learning opportunities and growth
 And more
 We are committed to providing accommodations for persons with disabilities. If you require accommodation, we will work with you to meet your needs.
